text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the rice farming and livestock exposure are significant. Can you confirm if the rash has spread to your soles, and do you notice any scaling or hyperpigmentation on the palms? Additionally, have you experienced any shortness of breath or cough?

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative tissue transglutaminase and anti-HLA results make Celiac disease unlikely. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urinary porphyrins and porphobilinogen levels effectively rule out acute porphyria. Given your history of working in flooded rice paddies and livestock exposure, combined with a pruritic rash, palm numbness, and negative autoimmune, infectious, and metabolic workups, have you experienced any visual disturbances like color blindness or significant fatigue?
